correctness.rationale: For graph-distance balls and counting measure, the nonlinear maximal norm squared is exactly the maximum of lambda_max(A^T A) over nonnegative row-selection averaging matrices, by choosing a maximizing ball at each output coordinate. Crucial {1,2} is NOT a ball in P4. Enumerated all 36 uncentered+18 centered P3 and 400 uncentered+144 centered P4 selection matrices from actual shortest-path ball definitions. Independently recomputed all 598 cases with exact rational leading-principal-minor Sylvester tests: P3 exceptional count1 in each family, P4 uncentered exactly2, centered exactly2. The P4 winners have Gram characteristic factors 324z^4-702z^3+308z^2-42z+1 over324 and z(36z^3-78z^2+35z-4)/36; their isolated top eigenvalues approximately 1.6322007547 and 1.6036000274. All excluded selections have squared norm less than 13/8 or 8/5; winning positive Perron eigenvectors yield the stated extremizing rays and reflections, with independent coordinate signs irrelevant. One/two/three vertex connected graphs show no split. Finite exact exhaustion proves the finite graph order claim, not just an experiment.
